title: Career Finder production workspace creation and empty account export

hosted.identityBasis: Previously recorded deployment identity; the browser does not independently expose the source commit.

method: Use the retained authenticated browser session and ordinary site controls; inspect the account page and downloaded JSON. No authentication bypass or direct browser-cookie extraction.

observations.action: Open the account page in a fresh tab
observations.result: Authenticated session retained; no cloud workspace initially existed.

observations.action: Use Create connection code on the signed-in connection page
observations.result: One-time-code panel and replace control appeared after the pending state, without a reported UI error. The credential value is omitted from this evidence.
Workspace controls loaded; zero connected phones, CVs, opportunities, reviews and application records were shown.

observations.action: Download account records through the visible account link
observations.result: Download completed and parsed as schema-version-1 JSON with a nonempty workspace identifier and account email. Identifier and email values are omitted from this evidence.

exportValidation.scope: Blank/default profile export. Export of populated profiles, CV metadata, review snapshots and application records is not established by this check.

remainingChecks: Native phone pairing and same-account recovery on another phone
Deliberate matching-email profile and PDF save
Populated account export, device revocation, interrupted-upload recovery and deletion
Publisher signing, store disclosures and distribution
Employer-authorized connector before live application submission
dataHandling: This public record omits account identifiers, names, email values, connection codes, session credentials, screenshots and the private export. The workspace and its data were retained; no destructive test was performed.
releaseImpact: Production workspace creation and inbound account export only. Hosted source/deployment, app builds, store records and employer systems were not changed by these browser checks.
